record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For n > 5, characterize all extreme rays of COP_n, the cone of real symmetric n x n copositive matrices A satisfying x^T A x >= 0 for every vector x in R_+^n. A matrix A in a convex cone K generates an extreme ray when every decomposition A = B + C with B and C in K forces B and C to be scalar multiples of A.

evidence.quote: It is an open question to characterize the extreme rays of COPn for n > 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{COP}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices $A$ that are copositive, i.e.
$$x^\top A x \ge 0 \quad \text{for every } x \in \mathbb{R}_+^n.$$
A nonzero matrix $A$ in a convex cone $K$ is said to generate an extreme ray of $K$ if for every decomposition $A = B + C$ with $B, C \in K$, both $B$ and $C$ are nonnegative scalar multiples of $A$.

For each integer $n > 5$, give an explicit characterization of all matrices $A \in \mathrm{COP}_n$ that generate extreme rays of $\mathrm{COP}_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The extreme rays of $\mathrm{COP}_5$ were characterized by Hildebrand (2012), and the extreme rays of $\mathrm{COP}_6$ were fully classified by Afonin–Hildebrand–Dickinson (2021). For $n \ge 7$ no complete characterization is known; the general problem remains open, although the non-exceptional extreme rays are well understood in arbitrary dimension.

status_evidence.title: Exploring the Exceptional Extreme Rays of the Copositive Cone
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis exploring exceptional extreme rays; full characterization for higher n not available.
